verdicts.verdict: declined - the canonical Usage open command is cmd.nav.open_usage_subject
verdicts.rationale: Packet section 06 lists this as a candidate to adjudicate. It is declined, and the concept's current aliasing is the direction canon forbids. Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md:8159 states verbatim: 'cmd.chat.open_thread_context_details, cmd.chat.focus_thread_context_details, and cmd.chat.close_thread_context_details remain the thread Context Detail Pane commands; they are not aliases for app-wide Usage.' :777 fixes that command's payload at { thread_id }, layout and UI state only, for the Chat context hover module and artifact deep-links. :8163 adds that run-only, thread-only or timestamp-only payloads cannot satisfy the primary Usage route identity when usage_event_ref is available, and :8150 designates cmd.nav.open_usage_subject as the Usage route and open command with route_target.object_kind 'usage_event'. Plans/usage-feature.md:67 independently retires run_id, thread_id and timestamp as canonical navigation. The concept nevertheless dispatches cmd.chat.open_thread_context_details from the Usage run inspector at u11-rundetail.js, the cmd.chat.open_thread_context_details dispatch in open(runId) with { surface: 'run_detail', id: runId } - a Usage surface, a run-only payload, no thread_id. cmd.nav.open_usage_subject is now dispatched by the run inspector at u11-rundetail.js, the cmd.nav.open_usage_subject call (corrected 2026-08-18: this register previously said it was dispatched nowhere, which was true when written and false after the remediation landed the dispatch) (68 occurrences under Plans/ excluding _shards, measured 2026-08-18).
verdicts.correct_disposition: No new id is minted. The Usage run inspector's open must move to cmd.nav.open_usage_subject with a usage-subject payload. cmd.chat.open_thread_context_details stays in place for its legitimate use at u11-context.js, the cmd.chat.open_thread_context_details dispatch, which does pass { thread_id }. This is a concept-side change and has not been made; the register records the ruling, not a repair.

CONFLICT FLAG: two candidate families point at one affordance — the canonical command owner should adjudicate which ID survives; recommend keeping cmd.chat.open_thread_context_details (already wired in three concepts) and retiring the alias.

retraction.why_the_claim_was_false: It recommended keeping exactly the aliasing UI_Command_Catalog.md:8159 prohibits, and cited no canon clause at all - so a reader had no way to see that the recommendation contradicted active canon, and the correct third option (cmd.nav.open_usage_subject) was invisible.

segment_count_ruling.ruling: The id is legal. There is no segment cap in canon.
segment_count_ruling.why_this_ruling_exists: A rule was asserted during the port handoff that 'Plans/DRY_Rules.md normalizes command ids to two segments', which would have made cmd.usage.forecast.request inadmissible. No such rule exists.
evidence: Plans/DRY_Rules.md:2109 is the heading 'Shared-runtime command-name normalization boundary'. The block at :2109-2130 is a dedup and owner-routing table - a two-column mapping of packet candidate names onto canonical dispositions - and it says of itself at :2111 that 'DRY normalization does not register commands or aliases.' It normalizes toward three-segment ids in several rows (cmd.worktree.provision to cmd.git.worktree.create). It is not a segment-count rule.

Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md:1450 UCC-006 'Command Id Naming Rules' is the real rule. Its canonical_text reads in full: 'UI command IDs must be lowercase, dot-separated, and prefixed with cmd.' No segment cap.
Plans/Wiring_Matrix.schema.json:75 pattern is ^cmd\\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)*$ - unbounded in segment count.
Measured 2026-08-18 over Plans/Wiring_Matrix.production.json: 668 distinct ui_command_id values, of which 245 carry three or more segments after the cmd. prefix (230 with three, 15 with four).

verdicts.verdict: blocked - cmd.nav.open_usage_subject already owns usage-subject opens
verdicts.rationale: New, backing the account row's 'Open provider console' (u11-widgets.js, the cmd.provider.usage.open_management dispatch). It is an open and route action, not a purchase command: packet section 06 requires real typed commands with confirmation and a receipt for purchase, pack, reset and reload execution, and opening a provider page is explicitly not that. But the id is blocked on genuine DRY grounds rather than on segment count: cmd.nav.open_usage_subject already owns usage-subject opens (68 occurrences under Plans/ excluding _shards, measured 2026-08-18), and Plans/DRY_Rules.md:2123 routes cmd.context.receipt.open by subject kind to cmd.nav.open_subject or cmd.nav.open_usage_subject. Minting a second family for the same job is the duplication that table exists to prevent.
verdicts.correct_disposition: Re-express the affordance on cmd.nav.open_usage_subject, or obtain a documented exception from the command owner. Not done; this register records the ruling only.

retraction.why_the_claim_was_false: The first half stands and is retained below as its own verdict: initial acquisition is an explicit user-triggered setup action, not a dispatched command. The second half was false. 'semantic.deep_link' was not a command - it was a locally invented pseudo-command, and its payload { surface, manager, section, focus_reason } named destinations that do not exist. Plans/settings_inventory.json has 12 categories and neither 'providers' nor 'usage' is one of them: 'providers' exists only as a subgroup of web, meaning web-search providers, and 'usage' only as a subgroup of ai. The tokens focus_reason, usage_and_extra_usage, usage_quick_controls and see_all have zero occurrences anywhere under Plans/ (measured 2026-08-18). Naming an invented envelope in a register of canonical command dispositions documented nothing.

retraction.why_the_claim_was_false: The counts were not reproducible to the stated figures and the method string did not pin enough to make them reproducible. It named neither the tree state, nor whether occurrences or matching lines were being counted, nor whether _shards were included - and _shards changes four of the six figures. The independent audit measured 29 / 29 / 24 / 21 / 2 / 2 at the closest 2026-08-11 commit and 43 or 35 / 43 or 35 / 31 or 25 / 39 or 34 / 5 or 4 / 5 or 4 on the working tree, against the published 32 / 32 / 25 / 20 / 2 / 2. Four of the six reproduce only approximately under any reading. Numbers presented as measurements must be re-derivable by a third party from the stated method alone.
retraction.what_is_unchanged: The census conclusion and every owner attribution in it verified exactly, both in the audit and again on 2026-08-18: UCC-116 exists at Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md:8838; catalog.usage_refresh, catalog.usage_export, catalog.account_select_profile and catalog.provider_switch_route all exist in Plans/Wiring_Matrix.production.json; the FinalGUISpec rate_limit CTA row is at FinalGUISpec.md:28909 as described. Only the numbers were unsound.

source_citation_policy: Source citations into u11-prism.html, u11-data.js, u11-widgets.js, u11-rundetail.js and u11-context.js name a symbol, identifier or exact string rather than a line number. Those five files were under concurrent edit on 2026-08-18 - u11-data.js moved twice while this repair was being written - so a line number here would be wrong by the time it was read. Line numbers are retained only for files that are stable in this pass: everything under Plans/ and under _shared/. Text preserved inside a `retraction` or `retracted_claim` object is left exactly as it was written, line numbers included, because its purpose is to record what a document said on a past date.
